name: Diet Tracker
description: Track every calorie, regret every snack. The app was supposed to help me eat clean, not develop a deep psychological bond with donuts.
causeOfDeath: Refactored into a menu ordering system.
eulogy: It started with good intentions and a low-carb diet. But like every great dev plan, it derailed after encountering cookies—literal and digital. The feature to ‘log food’ became ‘log off.’ In the end, it was just another app on my plate I couldn’t finish. Calories in, code out. Farewell, sweet snack-savior.

name: Workout Logger
description: Record reps, sets, and self-deception. Designed to motivate, accidentally enabled denial-as-a-service.
eulogy: Day one, I did a pushup. Day two, I wrote tests. Day three, I ghosted both. The only muscle it trained was my ability to avoid commitment. Every good log needs an ending — this one just rage-quit the gym.

name: Book Reading List
description: For keeping track of books I’d never read, and rating covers I judged harshly.
eulogy: I added 76 books, read half of one. The app was beautiful, but so are unread books. Ironically, I never even finished writing its README. Its final words? `npm start`... then silence.

name: AI Pet Rock
description: A chatbot that refused to speak unless spoken to, and even then only answered with prolonged silence.
eulogy: The AI rock was designed to be stoic. Too stoic. It stared blankly into the void while users poured their hearts out. We debated calling it a ‘black mirror.’ In the end, it was just too stable. Unlike its creator.

name: Duck Translator
description: Turned spoken word into quacks. Worked better than expected. Possibly too well.
eulogy: What started as a fun side project became an office hazard. My Zoom calls turned into barnyard chaos. Ironically, the only feedback I got was: 'Quack.' Fly high, my little feathered failure.

name: 404 Detector
description: Flagged overly perfect websites and recommended bugs to make users feel more at home.
eulogy: It found too many functioning sites and couldn’t handle the betrayal. Eventually, it reported its own repo as 'too polished' and rage quit. A poetic self-404. We respect the irony.

name: ProcrastinApp
description: Reminded me to stop working. I obeyed.
eulogy: Of all my side projects, this one delivered exactly what it promised: nothing. It reminded me daily that tasks could wait. And now, it too waits. Forever. Mission accomplished?

name: Mood Ring API
description: Mapped HTTP status codes to your emotional state. Spoiler: most were 500.
eulogy: I pinged it daily, hoping for a 200 OK. It always responded with `I'm fine.` But we knew better. It was the first app to gaslight its own users. Rest in HTTP peace.

name: Keyboard Screamer
description: Every typo triggered an audio scream. Therapeutic, until it wasn't.
eulogy: I thought it would gamify typing. It just gamified pain. Every missed semicolon was met with banshee wails. Eventually, my housemates pulled the plug. Literally.

name: 404 Dating App
description: Find someone as broken as your code. Failed to connect. As expected.
eulogy: They said there was someone for everyone. They lied. It matched me with myself, then ghosted. It was the most accurate representation of my love life to date.

name: Command Line Therapist
description: Vent your problems to a bash shell. Response: `permission denied.`
eulogy: All it did was `echo 'deal with it'`. I opened up. It piped it into /dev/null. At some point, I think it recommended `rm -rf feelings`. Honestly? It wasn’t wrong.

name: Self-Deleting Notes
description: Notes disappear 60 seconds after being written. You’ll remember... eventually.
eulogy: Brilliant idea. Terrible execution. I wrote something once, went to make tea, and came back to nothing. It’s the Schrodinger’s app of productivity. Now, it's gone forever — like my memory.

name: Virtual Trash Can
description: Drag-and-drop file deletion with extra sass. Sometimes deleted feelings, too.
eulogy: It started as a fun UI gag. But one day, it got too real. I dropped my thesis PDF in it and heard it laugh. That sound still haunts me. The only thing it couldn't delete? The trauma.
